correctness.rationale: Exact integer prime sieve enumerates all odd primes up to floor(2^(3m/4)); every unordered prime pair, including repeats, is visited; a bitmap indexed by all 2^(m-1) odd classes is exhaustive. All 21 exponents were checked with verified exact missing counts; the previously uncovered 745135 is proved impossible below 50923 by inverse testing and attained by 50923*7757. No infinite inference.

originality.rationale: Reviewed published primary text arXiv:2610.19597v1 and arXiv:2609.37434v1; asymptotic almost-all coverage for prime powers and random-model Θ>3/4 do not imply the exact true-prime finite endpoint. Own prior q/2 first successes (q=96 and q=256) differ in restriction and cannot imply new threshold. published-finding corpus searches and public web searches showed no dominating computation. Unindexed tables remain a named residual risk.
residual_risks: An unindexed numerical table could already give the same dyadic endpoint.
The Matomäki--Teräväinen older paper was compared from its primary abstract rather than reviewed in complete full text; no plausible indication of this finite endpoint appeared.

value.rationale: Three quarters is a sharp, explicitly motivated limit of the Granville-model hyperbola estimate, not an arbitrary parameter. The first true-prime dyadic all-unit-class coverage at this exponent, exact sharp prime bound 50923, and three excluded classes for 2^20 are a natural finite calibration for the open EOS prime-product problem; no broader theorem is claimed.
